Although rumors outside suggest that the iPhone 18 Pro starts at US$1,399, this claim may be exaggerated; however, a significant price hike for this year's new phone series is almost an inevitable reality.

Apple has earlier laid the groundwork for the price increase through its brand-new Apple Upgrade program, and now T-Mobile has responded by launching a new three-year installment plan...

Back in June this year, facing a sharp rise in memory costs, Apple raised prices on most of its products. Existing iPhone models were not affected at the time, but it is certain that the pricing of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be higher than last year's equivalent models.

The Apple Upgrade leasing program allows users to use various Apple products, including the iPhone, at a lower monthly fee. However, the biggest catch is that users do not own the product after the payment period ends, which may trap many customers in an endless cycle of Apple Upgrade leases.

T-Mobile will launch a brand-new installment plan tomorrow, allowing customers to spread the cost of their iPhone and all related fees over three years instead of two. The plan, called EIP Flex 36, is marketed by the company with zero interest and zero down payment.

It is worth noting the conditions attached to both offers: zero down payment and zero interest only apply to customers with good credit ratings. The terms also state that the actual annual percentage rate (APR) for some customers may be as high as 24%. However, if you qualify and plan to keep your phone for three years or more, this plan could be quite attractive.
